faq: Do you fix the problems you find?
The audit is a report, not a repair. You can use it with your own developer, or order one of our fix packages for the items you choose.
A staging copy or read only admin access is enough for most checks. We never change anything during an audit, and we never ask for your password.
Can you audit an old Drupal 7 site?
Yes. We include the end of support status and a plain upgrade path in the report, so you know your options and how much work each involves.
Do you check security in depth?
We check settings, roles, update status and known risky modules. A full penetration test is a specialist job and is outside this audit. We say so clearly in the report.

desc:
A Drupal site audit and fix list shows you what is wrong with your site and what to repair first. Ecom Swift LLC reviews security, speed, content and editing, then sends a written report ranked by importance and effort.

## What is a Drupal site audit?

A Drupal site audit is a structured review of a live Drupal site from three points of view: the visitor, the editor and the developer. It checks the Drupal version and update status, installed modules and themes, user roles, performance, mobile display, search basics and how easy it is to publish. The result is a report that tells you what to fix, in what order, and how.

Drupal sites age quietly. Modules fall behind, editors work around problems, and pages grow slower. An audit turns those vague worries into a list you can act on.

## Why an audit comes before spending

Without a review, money tends to go to whatever feels urgent rather than what matters. A team may redesign the theme while an outdated module leaves a security hole. Another may pay for a speed plugin while the real cause is a heavy view or oversized images.

A ranked fix list stops that. It separates quick wins from large projects, so you can decide what to do yourself, what to give to your developer and what to ask us to do later.

## How an audit improves results

The mechanism is simple: problems found early are cheaper to fix. A security gap closed before it is used costs an hour, while a hacked site costs far more. A slow page that frustrates visitors affects enquiries, sign-ups and search visibility, so finding the cause protects those. An editing process that confuses staff wastes their time every week, and fixing the form or the role setup gives that time back.

An audit also gives you a record. When you talk to a developer or a vendor, you can hand over specific findings instead of a general complaint.

## What a good Drupal audit covers

- Core and module versions, and which updates are pending.
- Security settings, user roles and permissions, and accounts that should not exist.
- Page speed on a sample of important pages, with the likely causes of slowness.
- Installed modules and themes, including unused or abandoned ones.
- The editor experience: content forms, media handling and publishing steps.
- Search basics such as page titles, descriptions, headings and the sitemap.
- Mobile display and layout problems.
- Error logs and broken links.
- For a deeper audit, a sample of custom code and an accessibility check of key pages.
- A ranked list of findings, each with a screenshot and plain fix steps.

## What we do

We start with a read only review, using the access level you choose to give us. We run tests on a sample of pages, go through the admin area as an editor would, and note each problem with evidence. We then rank every finding by importance and effort, and write the steps to fix it in language your team can follow.

The Basic package is a quick health check with a short summary. Standard adds a module and theme review, an editor review and a longer action plan. Premium adds a code sample review, an accessibility check, a call to walk through the report and a plan for the following month. We audit and report only: fixes are a separate job, and we can quote them once you have read the list.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Tell us which pages, forms or processes matter most to your business.
- Share known problems and past incidents, so we check them first.
- Read the report with your developer and assign each finding an owner.
- Fix high impact items first, even when they are dull.
- Repeat the audit after major changes.

**Avoid:**
- Treating the report as a one-time document and filing it away.
- Fixing low priority cosmetic items while a security finding waits.
- Sharing admin passwords by email.
- Assuming an old site is fine because nothing has visibly broken.
- Making big changes on the live site while the audit is under way.

## Who this is for

This suits an organization that inherited a Drupal site from a previous agency and does not know its state. It also suits a marketing team that feels the site is slow or hard to edit but cannot explain why. A business planning a redesign or migration will find it useful as a starting inventory.

## What we need from you

We need the site address and an account for us with read only or reviewer rights, set up as a collaborator, team or staff user. We never ask for your password. Add a few lines about your goals and any complaints from editors or visitors. After you order, we send a short checklist and deliver the report with an optional walk-through call.
